name: RoboBench
description: RoboBench is a benchmark that systematically evaluates multimodal large language models (MLLMs) as embodied brains for robotic manipulation. It defines five dimensions—instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis—spanning 14 capabilities, 25 tasks, and 6092 QA pairs. The benchmark includes diverse embodiments, attribute-rich objects, multi-view scenes, and memory-driven navigation, drawing from large-scale real robotic data and in-house collection. It also introduces an MLLM-as-world-simulator evaluation framework for assessing long-horizon planning.
creator: Yulin Luo, Chun-Kai Fan, Menghang Dong, Jiayu Shi, Mengdi Zhao, Bo-Wen Zhang, Cheng Chi, Jiaming Liu, Gaole Dai, Rongyu Zhang, Ruichuan An, Kun Wu, Zhengping Che, Shaoxuan Xie, Guocai Yao, Zhongxia Zhao, Pengwei Wang, Guang Liu, Zhongyuan Wang, Tiejun Huang, Shanghang Zhang
publisher: Peking University, Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence, Fudan University, University of Science and Technology Beijing, Beijing Innovation Center of Humanoid Robotics
rai:dataCollection: Datasets were built from open-source and in-house robotic data, enriched with MLLM- and human-provided annotations. Data combine large-scale real-world robotic datasets with curated in-house collection. Sources include: robotic-centric data using real robot data with type and view metadata; object-centric data combining curated static attributes with GPT-generated functional properties; scene-centric data leveraging Gemini-segmented video steps; task-centric data with human-labeled bounding boxes; planning data from high-quality robotic videos; affordance data from sampled representative frames; and failure analysis data from RoboMIND with expert labels plus synthesized planning failures.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Web Scraping
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Due to lack of real-world planning failure data, planning-level failures are synthesized by perturbing correct instructions (wrong object, missing step, wrong order).
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Large-scale real-world robotic datasets including RH20T (Fang et al., 2023), Open X-Embodiment (Collaboration et al., 2023), RDT-1B (Liu et al., 2024b), data from Liu et al. (2024c), RoboMIND (Wu et al., 2024), AgiBot World (Bu et al., 2025), EmbodiedGPT (Mu et al., 2023), data scaling laws dataset (Lin et al., 2024a), Thinking in Space (Yang et al., 2024), and in-house collected robotic manipulation videos.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Explicit instructions are rewritten into implicit (demand-based) forms using LLMs. Planning-level failure data is synthesized by perturbing correct instructions with wrong object, missing step, or wrong order modifications. Natural language step descriptions are mapped to predefined function sequences. Function arguments are instantiated with objects extracted from step descriptions.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A two-stage quality control process is applied: (1) data filtering during construction using general criteria (image quality, task validity) and task-specific filters (e.g., excluding single-arm data from dual-arm tasks); (2) post-construction validation by 20 professionally trained annotators checking linguistic clarity, answerability, and correctness. A majority-vote strategy is also applied: items all models solve correctly are removed, and items all models fail are manually reviewed and corrected. All data are standardized into multiple-choice QA or structured planning formats.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were created through multiple methods: (1) Gemini generated structured annotations for planning tasks including task summaries, step-wise instructions with timestamps, and metadata (objects, actions, scenes, embodiments), refined by human annotators; (2) human annotators labeled bounding boxes for task-centric perception; (3) human annotators provided relative position and keypoint change annotations for spatial and causal reasoning; (4) experts labeled execution-level failures from RoboMIND; (5) GPT generated functional properties and distractors for object-centric data; (6) template-based QA was used for robotic-centric data; (7) human-annotated directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) capture inter-step dependencies for planning evaluation; (8) 20 professionally trained annotators conducted quality inspections validating linguistic clarity, answerability, and correctness.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A majority-vote strategy is used: items that all models solve correctly are removed (too easy), whereas items all models fail to solve undergo manual review and correction. For planning evaluation, expert annotators assigned holistic scores (0-20) referencing ground-truth planning lists and considering skill selection, object identification, and plan executability. Pearson correlation between automated metrics and human scores was computed to validate metric alignment.
rai:dataSocialImpact: RoboBench provides a comprehensive scaffold to quantify high-level cognition, clarify the role of the embodied brain, and guide the development of next-generation MLLMs toward more robust robotic intelligence. It aims to advance embodied AI for robotic manipulation in dynamic, unstructured environments.
rai:dataBiases: Planning data primarily focuses on concrete action execution without explicitly distinguishing between left-right arm assignments or positional movements, which may bias cross-embodiment planning evaluation. Performance drops sharply when tasks involve uncommon objects, suggesting the benchmark may reflect biases toward common, well-seen objects in existing robotic datasets.
rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark relies on synthesized planning-level failure data due to lack of real-world planning failure examples. Execution-level failure diagnosis is intrinsically difficult, with even human evaluators achieving only 47.30 on this dimension. The benchmark focuses on manipulation tasks and may not generalize to other embodied AI domains.
rai:dataUseCases: RoboBench is designed for evaluating (testing) multimodal large language models as embodied brains for robotic manipulation. It supports benchmarking across five cognitive dimensions: instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis. It can be used to establish leaderboards and provide actionable insights for advancing embodied AI development.
rai:annotatorDemographics: 20 professionally trained annotators conducted quality inspections. No further demographic details are provided.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Gemini (Comanici et al., 2025) for structured annotation generation (task summaries, step-wise instructions, timestamps, metadata); GPT for generating functional properties and distractors for object-centric data; LLMs for rewriting explicit instructions into implicit forms; detection models for annotation assistance.
